mutate_comment: The .ts layers (utils, hooks, use-cases, services, repositories, the IPC schemas) hold the app's logic and are mutated wholesale. Components are not, since most of their mutants are UI text the tests reasonably do not assert. The exceptions are named one by one, the components that gate a destructive action (the delete confirmation, the database section and the library folder section). Measure a candidate on its own before adding it, and check a .tsx survivor by hand first, because perTest can credit a mutant to another file's tests and report a survivor that the file's own tests kill.
tauri_client_comment: src/lib/tauri-client.ts is left out on purpose. perTest does not credit the streamLiveChatFile tests to it, so its mutants show as uncovered although the tests exist. It can go in once that attribution is fixed.
coverageAnalysis_comment: perTest runs only the tests that cover each mutant. With 'off' every mutant re-runs the whole suite, and a full run no longer fits the scheduled job's timeout.
ignoreStatic_comment: A static mutant lives in module-level code, which perTest cannot attribute to a test, so each one re-runs the whole suite. They are about 1% of the mutants and most of the run time.
dryRunTimeoutMinutes_comment: The 5-minute default runs out before the dry run finishes, and a dry-run timeout aborts with no score. See the Stryker step in .github/workflows/mutation.yml.
thresholds_comment: break fails the scheduled run (.github/workflows/mutation.yml). It sits a few points under the score the CI runs measure, which leaves room for a new module whose tests are still catching up and still fails on a real loss of test strength. low is kept equal to break. Raise it only from a run that reached the end, since an aborted run has no score.
